observation.visible_scene: A single translucent, roughly dome-shaped ice cube rests centered on a mottled brown-and-grey granite/stone surface. A thin film and small puddle of clear meltwater sit at its base, with a cluster of tiny bright droplets/bubbles on the cube's right face. The background is heavily blurred (shallow depth of field), neutral grey-tan tones. The composition and framing stay constant across all sampled frames.
visible_changes: The ice cube remains in the same position and silhouette from t=0.000s to t=2.669s; no translation, rotation, or visible deformation of the cube is detectable.

The meltwater puddle at the base and the small droplet highlights on the right side of the cube persist in essentially the same size and location throughout the excerpt; no clear expansion or reduction is observable.
The specular highlights and overall lighting on the cube do not change appreciably.
No camera pan, tilt, zoom, or shift is evident; the scene is effectively static within this segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ice is melting at a rate too slow to register over this short window (the standing water implies an ongoing melt, but its onset and any later disappearance are outside the excerpt).
The ambient temperature or heat source driving any melting.
Events before t=0 or after t=2.669s (e.g., further shrinkage or full dissipation of the cube).
uncertain_details: Any sub-frame change in puddle size or cube shape is below the visible resolution of these samples, so 'no change' describes what is observable, not necessarily what is physically happening.
Exact material identity of the surface and the cube (assumed ice on stone) is inferred from appearance only.
